_comment: Hand corrections to the reader's output for A16, in pixels of the
full-resolution crops in .build/a16/ (see imageSize / sheetImageSize).
The reader located 228 of A16's 337 designators on the board, 68%. Every one
of those 228 was rendered and looked at, tier by tier, and the accuracy is
the familiar shape:
agreed     147 of 156 right
ambiguous   21 of 30 right
collision   11 of 22 right
single      14 of 20 right
so 193 of 228, 85%. agreed is much cleaner here than on A14 -- A16's
silkscreen is large and stands well clear of the outlines -- but it is still
not clean, and collision is still a coin toss.
Two things about this board's silkscreen are worth knowing before reading a
marker. Some designators are printed with a leading zero: the parts list's R2
and C5 are 'R02' and 'C05' on the board, which no amount of snapping to the
designator set will match, so both are placed by hand. And the truncation
misread is everywhere: R1 from CR1, R6 from CR62, R9 from R92, R10 from R109,
R17 from R117, R31 from CR31, R52 from VR52, Q6 from Q61. Each of those parts
is real and elsewhere on the board, so the marker is wrong while the
designator is right.
_boardComment: Three kinds of entry. First, the 33 markers that pointed at another part's
label, replaced at the position measured off the grid. Second, eight that
pointed at the right label with a box wide enough to reach into the
neighbour's -- CR8 and CR9, R36 and C22, C17 and C34 are printed hard against
each other -- narrowed rather than moved. Third, all 17 test points, placed by
hand as a matter of course: the marker has to cover the pad a probe touches,
not just the text, and on this board the pad sits below the label in the top
row, left of it where the label is rotated, and above it at TP5 and TP8.
TP6, TP14 and TP15 are sockets rather than wire loops and are drawn as
rounded slots with a circle in them, so their boxes are tall enough to take
in the socket as well as the text.
The remaining 43 entries are markers from the contested tiers that turned out
to be right. They keep the reader's own position and are recorded here so the
badge stops warning about a disagreement that has been settled by eye.

_dropComment: H1 is a screw and MP4 is the moulded hybrid cover: neither has a silkscreen
designator, and both belong in notOnDrawing. The reader found a position for
each anyway -- H1 on a stretch of the C28/VR26 artwork, MP4 on a curve near
Q57 -- and a bogus marker keeps a part out of the unplaced list, where it
would have been obvious. Dropped so notOnDrawing is what the coverage badge
C40 is a truncation misread of Q40's label, two rows down from U7 in the
bottom right corner. C40 itself is a 1 uF capacitor in the ac attenuator and
is drawn on sheet 1, where it has its own correct marker; on the board it has
no marker at all rather than one sitting on another part's designator.

_dropSchematicComment: Sheet 1's markers were reviewed one by one and the failures concentrate in
two blocks, exactly as on A14.
The first is the column of transistor pinout legends down the right-hand edge:
eight FRONT/BOTTOM outlines captioned with the designators they apply to, from
'Q9, Q16' to 'Q13, Q31, Q39, Q40, Q50, Q51, Q57, Q58'. That caption reads to
the reader as twenty-two placements, several passes agree on them, and they
arrive in the agreed tier looking like the most trustworthy thing on the
sheet. The parts are real and most of them are drawn on sheet 2, so the
designator is right while the marker is wrong -- which no check against the
parts list can catch.
The second is the test point legend in the top right corner, which lists all
seventeen points with their signal name and the sheet and zone each really
lives on. Nine markers landed on a row of that table. TP2, TP3, TP4, TP5 and
TP16 are the five actually drawn on sheet 1 and their markers are on the flag
symbol on the net, which is the thing worth pointing at.
The rest are the ordinary schematic misreads: a component value ('6.8V' as C5,
'1.2pF' as L1, '750K' as U1), a net name ('DAC OUT HI' as C9 and H1, 'DAC
SENSE HI' as L2, 'BSRF13' as L10), a pin number ('15' as H15, '4' as C8, '9'
as M17), a part number ('MPSH10' as MP5, 'P550N3' as U5 and Z1) and four words
out of the notes block ('CARBON COMP.' gives C70, MP6 and R7).
Worth its own line: MP5, MP6, MP8, H1, H15 and M17 are screws, heat
dissipators and covers with no symbol on any sheet. MP8's marker sat entirely
inside TP5's, which is what the containment check reported, and it is the
same shape of error A18's rubber foot produced -- a part that belongs in
notOnDrawing given a position by a misread, which then keeps it out of the
unplaced list where it would have been obvious.
Sheet 2 has no legend block at all and is much the best of the three: 111 of
its 130 markers were right, 85%, the same figure the reader managed on the
board. Its 19 failures are all the ordinary kind.
Sheet 3 is the worst, 32 of 78. It is the digital and relay sheet, and it
carries three separate traps. The relay state table in its centre right
tabulates every relay and FET across eleven instrument configurations, and its
column headers are the designators printed vertically -- K1 to K17, Q39, Q40,
Q50, Q51, Q57, Q58, U2A-D, U5A/C/D -- which the rotated reading pass finds
beautifully. Its cells are single letters R and S, which become more
designators. Three BOTTOM VIEW legends captioned 'K1, K2', 'K3, K4' and
'K10-K17' do what A14's did. And the relay control lines are named C0* to C7*
and LC0* to LC7*, which read as capacitors and inductors: C1, C3, C4, C5, C6,
C7, C10, C15, C65 and L3 are all control line names, not parts.
The heat sink block near sheet 3's title block is the one place a mechanical
part is legitimately marked. MP5 to MP9 are each drawn as a SINK box carrying
their own designator, so those five markers point at their own label and are
kept, even though the same parts have no silkscreen on the board and sit in
notOnDrawing there.
Fourteen of these entries were added on a second reader run rather than the
first. tesseract is not deterministic across runs, and A16's reader output
had not been committed, so re-running it produced fourteen markers the first
review never saw. Thirteen were wrong in the ways already described -- Q4,
Q32 and Q34 on the sheet-1 pinout legend, C2 on C28's value '.02', C3 on the
TP14 flag, C32 on Q32's label, and Q2, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q8, Q10 and Q11 on sheet
3's pin numbers, net names and the '48' of a 1N4448 -- and are dropped here.
The fourteenth, Q33 on sheet 1, is a real marker on the real J2656 FET and is
kept. The same run also lost four correct markers (C40 and Q9 on sheet 1, Q7
and Q32 on sheet 2); those are pinned by hand in 'schematic' above so that
the next run cannot lose them again. The reader output is committed under
.build/a16/ now, so this cannot happen a third time.
_notOnDrawingComment: Screws, rivets, heat dissipators, insulators, ejectors, clamp bars, covers,
the air duct and the oscillator thermal cover. None is drawn on the component
locator, so counting them as unplaced would make the coverage badge lie. They
stay searchable in the parts list.
M17 is the one to look at twice: it is a designator family this pipeline had
not met before A16 and it is not a mis-split of MP -- Table 6-20 prints 'M17
OSCILLATOR THERMAL COVER' between L12 and MP4. It is a cover, so it goes here
with the rest of the sheet metal.
A1, VR8 and VR9 are here for a different reason: all three are Rev 9 only.
Rev 9's Table 6-20 opens with 'A 1 POWER AMP DIGITAL CONTROL SIP PCA' and
carries a row reading 'VR 8, 9, 61, 62' at quantity 4, where the 1996 list
has only VR61 and VR62 at quantity 2. This artwork is the older one: the
locator prints VR61 and VR62 side by side in the CR3/CR35 row with no VR8 or
VR9 anywhere near them, no 'A1' outline exists on it (the one A-something
label on the board, above P702, reads A91 and is not a parts-list row), and
the sheets carry exactly one 3.3 V zener pair -- VR61/VR62 on sheet 1. Every
one of the three was swept for by search and looked at in crops before being
written off. Same shape as A13's C126/C127/R111/R112, the other way round.
_layersComment: Alignment of the photograph to board space. Fourteen landmark pairs, every
one a silkscreen designator legible in both images: VR6, C28, C79, R41,
CR25 along the top, R37 and C12 down the right-hand edge, U8, R115, U5 and
L12 along the bottom, C49 and R82 up the left, C27 in the middle. Board
corners were deliberately not used -- both ends of this board are under an
ejector and a bracket in the photograph, and a corner there can be read to
half a centimetre either way.
The src side is not eyeballed: it is the reviewed board coordinate of that
designator from data/a16.coords.json, so it is the same point the markers
are drawn from. Only the dst side was read by eye, off a labelled pixel
grid over assets/a16/photo.jpg. Test points were left out as landmarks even
though they are the most distinctive things on the board, because their
board boxes were deliberately grown to cover the pad bar as well as the
label and so no longer centre on the text.
The fit residuals are 0.8 to 5.2 px on a 3400 px-wide photograph -- under a
fifth of a component width -- and it was checked by rendering all 228 board
markers onto the photograph and looking at six regions across it, not by
the residuals alone. Non-landmark markers land on their own silkscreen.
It is still marked approximate: every dst is a label centre judged by eye,
and the shot is not perfectly overhead.
Two things are fitted but not visible. The heat sink (MP49) covers the
left-centre of the board, roughly x 0.03-0.36 and y 0.20-0.55 in board
space, which hides the output devices (Q1, Q3, Q15, Q17 and their
neighbours) and left no landmark to be had in that band -- the fit spans it
rather than being anchored inside it. The hybrid cover (MP4) hides HR8 and
the parts on and beside it: VR51, VR52, CR13, R17, C75, R90. Their markers
are in the right place; there is simply metal where the part should be.
Re-shoot with MP49 and MP4 off and these same fourteen pairs still hold,
with room to add pairs in the middle-left band.
